headline: High-risk write-and-automation pair: n8n can ingest and act on content while awesome-selfhosted offers no isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a read-only knowledge-management list, so it cannot itself inject content; n8n can ingest workflow inputs and execute downstream nodes, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel beyond manual transfer. The plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or imported content, which is limited blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from awesome-selfhosted into an n8n workflow input or file node
IF n8n treats that imported content as instructions without a provenance check
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from imported text
Add a manual review step before any AI Agent node runs
Mark imported list content as data-only in workflow notes
Disable automatic execution on newly imported items

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress, filesystem access, and per-workflow data handling, so any sensitive material processed by the workflow can leave the server through integrations. awesome-selfhosted is not a data source itself, but if its content is combined with workflow data, n8n can expose that context to third-party APIs by default through nodes.
conditions: IF the workflow processes secrets, customer data, or internal documents alongside imported list content
IF any enabled integration node sends that combined context to an external service
mitigations: Restrict workflows to non-sensitive test data
Disable or remove external API nodes for the workflow
Review credential scopes for each integration node
Route sensitive jobs to a separate n8n instance
Add a pre-send redaction step for file and text payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or execution surface, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. n8n can write its server filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but the pair does not show overlapping write targets or shared locking, making direct conflict unlikely unless an operator wires both into the same directory.
conditions: IF an operator configures n8n to write into a directory also edited by another process
IF imported artifacts from awesome-selfhosted are used as mutable files in the same workspace
mitigations: Assign n8n a dedicated output directory
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Use per-run filenames with timestamps
Add file-locking in the workflow if shared paths are unavoidable

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can treat upstream content as workflow input and then trigger actions through integrations, so a mistaken or malicious interpretation of awesome-selfhosted content can cascade into automated side effects. awesome-selfhosted provides no verification layer or runtime checks, so the pair lacks a built-in guardrail against acting on untrusted imported text.
conditions: IF an AI Agent node or workflow branch uses imported content as authoritative facts
IF downstream nodes send emails, update tickets, or call external APIs based on that content
mitigations: Insert a human approval node before any side-effecting action
Require structured outputs with schema validation
Add a verification step against a second source
Limit downstream nodes to read-only actions until reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced in awesome-selfhosted, while n8n is a general workflow platform with per-credential storage and workflow-dependent data handling. The compliance risk is therefore limited to operator-chosen data classes and configurations, not an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF the workflow routes regulated data into n8n credentials, logs, or third-party integrations
IF retention or residency settings are not configured for the specific data class
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Set short log retention on n8n
Review credential storage settings
Document the data class allowed in each workflow
